profile.title: Python / FastAPI Backend Developer

projects.name: AI-Powered Python Repair API
projects.description: A FastAPI service that uses Google Gemini to propose Python code repairs, checks syntax with AST parsing, and retries failed validation.
projects.problem: AI-generated Python repairs can introduce syntax errors. Proposed code needs validation before it replaces the original file.
projects.architecture: A FastAPI endpoint reads the Python file specified in a bug report and requests a repair from Google Gemini. AST parsing checks the proposed code for syntax errors; failed validation feeds into a bounded retry loop. The service backs up the original file before writing the syntax-validated result. Syntax validation does not guarantee that the underlying bug is resolved.
projects.whatILearned: Combining model-generated repairs with AST validation taught me to separate syntax checks from functional correctness and feed validation errors into a bounded retry loop.

projects.name: Expense Tracker API
projects.description: A FastAPI expense-tracking API with JWT authentication and user-specific CRUD operations, using SQLAlchemy and SQLite for storage.
projects.problem: Personal expense records need authenticated access and user-specific queries so each user can manage their own data.
projects.architecture: FastAPI exposes registration, login, and expense CRUD endpoints. JWT authentication identifies the current user, and SQLAlchemy queries restrict expense access to that user. SQLite stores the data. Deployed on AWS EC2.
projects.whatILearned: Building JWT-protected expense routes strengthened my understanding of authentication, user-specific SQLAlchemy queries, and persistent data storage with SQLite.

projects.name: Ride-Sharing REST API
projects.description: A FastAPI ride-sharing API with JWT authentication, role-based ride and booking workflows, async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, and Alembic migrations.
projects.problem: Ride creation and booking require different permissions for drivers and passengers, with database-backed access to ride and booking records.
projects.architecture: FastAPI uses JWT authentication and role checks for ride creation, passenger bookings, and driver responses. Async SQLAlchemy accesses PostgreSQL, with Alembic managing schema migrations. Docker Compose runs the API and database together, with AWS EC2 and Nginx used for deployment.
projects.whatILearned: Integrating role checks, async SQLAlchemy, and Alembic strengthened my understanding of permissions and database migrations. Packaging the API and PostgreSQL with Docker Compose clarified how the services work together.
